title: Finish fingerprint setup when a print is already enrolled
head: 2b24db055dbf
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates
outcome: changes suggested: fresh print failing verification still advises re-enrolling though a rerun now skips enrollment (reproduced); fingerprint-package-test.sh lacks an fprintd-list stub and fails on hosts with a print enrolled (reproduced); enroll-duplicate premise contradicted by fprintd source (not reproduced, collapsed); optional PAM test improvement (surviving mutant); related PRs #13467/#13612

leads.summary: All-device enrollment check does not match the default device used by verification
leads.consequence: With two readers and a saved print only on the non-default reader, fprintd-list emits an entry, so setup skips enrollment. fprintd-verify selects the default reader, finds no enrolled fingers and fails; no PAM is written, setup suggests deleting the saved prints. A retry sees the same entry and repeats. This can also leave a mismatch with PAM, which selects a device by number of the user's enrolled prints rather than the fprintd-verify default. Match print detection and verification to the device actually intended for authentication, or handle a no-print default explicitly.
leads.triage: behavioural; Opus follow-up Q2 (opus/followup-1.md): converges after fprintd-delete and rerun, but deletes a usable print on a non-default reader; rare hardware, source-only; not published

leads.summary: A failed list query is treated as absence, while a failed verify advises wiping all prints
leads.consequence: If list cannot reach D-Bus, has an authorization error, or fails after printing a first device's entry, its status is ignored because the predicate only returns grep's exit status. Empty/error output sends a previously enrolled user to another fprintd-enroll (which may fail as duplicate), while a partial entry can skip enrollment despite an error. For an existing print, any later verify error (busy, no device, wrong finger, no match) yields the blanket fprintd-delete $USER recommendation. fprintd-delete enumerates and deletes every saved print on all devices for the named account, unnecessarily destroys valid enrolled data for temporary/usage failures, and does not fix the underlying device. Distinguish list failure from no print, classify verify failure and offer deletion only after diagnosing an unusable print.
leads.triage: list failure falls back to the base enroll path (Opus confirmed); retry-vs-delete wording is in Opus optional notes; not published

leads.summary: The new branch never tells a user with a non-index print which finger the verifier selects
leads.consequence: If a user previously enrolled two fingers and touches the right index finger as the setup's old prompt suggests, fprintd-verify defaults to the first enrolled finger on that device, not necessarily right-index-finger. On a swipe reader a different enrolled finger yields no match; the script then instructs the user to delete ALL prints, although pam_fprintd can use 'any' finger and a good print exists. Explain which finger fprintd-verify asks for (or choose the desired finger explicitly) and don't equate one wrong swipe to a bad stored template.
leads.triage: already in Opus edge notes (fprintd-verify picks the first listed finger); low value, not published

leads.summary: New enrollment lookup trusts $USER, but verification uses the process's own identity
leads.consequence: If $USER is stale, unset or different from the calling account (for example after changing users), the new fprintd-list query checks the wrong account and either skips a needed enrollment or re-enrolls when the current account already has prints. sudo fprintd-enroll uses the supplied name, whereas bare fprintd-verify defaults to its invoking account. The error instructs deleting $USER's prints even though that might be another account. Resolve and validate the actual invoking account once and use the same account at every call; related open PR #8534 only changes the preexisting enrollment argument, so its resolution must also include the new lookup and advice.
leads.triage: $USER trust unchanged from base (Opus); PR #8534 overlap noted privately; not published

leads.summary: Existing package test now invokes an unstubbed real fprintd-list
leads.consequence: Each of the package test's setup invocations reaches the newly added fprintd-list call, but its fake bin provides only fprintd-enroll and fprintd-verify, not fprintd-list. Outside a sandbox it can contact the real system D-Bus and query the host's enrolled prints. A user with a fingerprint sees the test take the skip/verification path instead of the asserted enrollment path, so the package fixture fails depending on the host. Stub fprintd-list here to return a deterministic no-enrollment result, and add a no-host-access assertion.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (finding 2, package test lacks fprintd-list stub); corroboration, published

leads.summary: Multiple open fingerprint PRs edit exactly the new enrollment and verification hunks
leads.consequence: PRs #13467 and #13612 add different already-enrolled branches, and #10235 replaces the verify call with a bounded retry for busy devices. All are diverged (not stacked); merge-file against each PR's actual base produces conflict markers in this PR's changed lines. GitHub reports those PRs mergeable against their base, not against this PR. A future resolution must retain a single enrolled check, #13612's opt-in/fallback if intended, and #10235's retry instead of silently restoring the old call; #12480 also conflicts beside the new check and its device-readiness guard must be kept. This is a coordination warning, not a claim of a current base conflict. #13187 and #12833 can merge at the setup file without markers.
leads.triage: factual: #13467 conflicts (Opus conflict-check); #13612/#12480 already fail against quattro; #10235 open and touches setup (gh verified); #13467/#13612 published as related PRs

leads.summary: Enrolled-path test would pass if sudo and polkit PAM setup were removed
leads.consequence: Both success cases only check that sudo tee /etc/pam.d/omarchy-lock-fingerprint is logged; a plausible regression deleting setup_pam_config at production line 120 while retaining setup_lock_fingerprint_pam at 121 still passes every assertion. sudo and polkit remain without fingerprint authentication even while the test reports 'configures PAM'. Add checks that sudo sed wrote the sudo and polkit stacks (with isolated PAM fixtures, not the host's real /etc).
leads.triage: behavioural; Opus follow-up Q1 ran the mutant (review-4) and it survives on every simulated PAM state; published as Optional test improvement

leads.summary: Failure to verify an existing print returns success and the test discards its status
leads.consequence: After fprintd-verify returns nonzero, the new recovery branch's last echo succeeds and the script ends with status 0. The caller can report a successful setup while no PAM is installed, and a rerun repeats the same failure as long as the print remains. The test explicitly appends `|| true`, so neither it nor the package harness checks this. This also occurred for the old verify failure branch, but is still present on the new adopted-print failure path; add explicit exit 1 and assert it in the test.
leads.triage: pre-existing exit 0 on verification failure, in Opus edge notes; not published

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** A new print that fails verification still gets "try enrolling again", which a rerun now skips.

### Fresh print that fails verification gets the old advice

The `fprintd-delete` advice is printed only when `already_enrolled` is true, so a print enrolled in this run gets the old message. **Impact:** the rerun only re-verifies that print; the useful advice comes after a second failure.

**Suggested change:** merge the `elif $already_enrolled` and `else` branches so every verification failure gets the `fprintd-delete` advice.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at 2b24db05)</summary>

# Reproducer: fresh enrollment that fails verification still says "try enrolling again"

Reviewed head: `2b24db055dbf71cb5e152d3f131f36481ebda988`. Merge-base: `97a9fce54f5df007afe7b8637ddc09314f38ad00`.

A test in the PR's own style. The stubbed `fprintd-list` reports whatever the stubbed `fprintd-enroll` stored, as fprintd does. First run: nothing enrolled, enrollment works, `fprintd-verify` fails. Second run: the print from the first run is still there, so setup skips enrollment. The test fails if the first run's advice does not say how to enroll again under those conditions.

Save as `test/shell.d/fingerprint-setup-rerun-test.sh` and run from the repository root:

```bash
bash test/shell.d/fingerprint-setup-rerun-test.sh
```

```bash
#!/bin/bash
#
# A print that fresh enrollment stored is still enrolled when its verification
# fails, so the next run of setup skips enrollment. The advice printed after
# that failure has to work on the next run.

set -euo pipefail

source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

setup="$ROOT/bin/omarchy-setup-security-fingerprint"
scratch=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$scratch"' EXIT
mkdir -p "$scratch/bin"
export CALL_LOG="$scratch/calls"
export PRINTS="$scratch/prints"
export PATH="$scratch/bin:$ROOT/bin:$PATH"

stub() {
  printf '#!/bin/bash\n%s\n' "$2" > "$scratch/bin/$1"
  chmod +x "$scratch/bin/$1"
}

stub sudo '[[ $1 == fprintd-enroll ]] && exec "$@"; printf "sudo %s\n" "$*" >> "$CALL_LOG"'
stub omarchy-hw-fingerprint 'exit 0'
stub omarchy-pkg-missing 'exit 1'
# Like fprintd, list what an earlier fprintd-enroll stored.
stub fprintd-list 'if [[ -e $PRINTS ]]; then printf "Fingerprints for user %s on Validity VFS5011 (swipe):\n - #0: right-index-finger\n" "$1"; else printf "User %s has no fingers enrolled for Validity VFS5011.\n" "$1"; fi'
stub fprintd-enroll 'echo "fprintd-enroll $*" >> "$CALL_LOG"; touch "$PRINTS"'
stub fprintd-verify 'echo "fprintd-verify" >> "$CALL_LOG"; exit 1'

run_setup() {
  : > "$CALL_LOG"
  USER=tester bash "$setup" > "$scratch/out" 2>&1 || true
}

# First run: nothing enrolled, enrollment works, verification fails.
run_setup
grep -qx 'fprintd-enroll tester' "$CALL_LOG" || fail "the first run enrolls" "$(<"$CALL_LOG")"
first_run=$(sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' "$scratch/out")

# Second run: does setup enroll again, as the first run's advice suggests?
run_setup
if ! grep -q '^fprintd-enroll' "$CALL_LOG" && ! grep -q 'fprintd-delete tester' <<< "$first_run"; then
  fail "a fresh print that fails to verify says how to enroll again" \
    "first run said: $(grep -i 'verification failed' <<< "$first_run")
second run calls: $(tr '\n' ' ' < "$CALL_LOG")"
fi
pass "a fresh print that fails to verify says how to enroll again"
```

## Actual output at 2b24db05 (exit 1, stderr)

```
first run said: Verification failed. You may want to try enrolling again.
second run calls: fprintd-verify 
not ok - a fresh print that fails to verify says how to enroll again
```

## Actual output at the merge-base 97a9fce5 (exit 0)

```
ok - a fresh print that fails to verify says how to enroll again
```

(At the merge-base the second run enrolls again, so the old advice was accurate there.)

## With the suggested change

Replacing the `elif $already_enrolled; then ... else ... fi` tail with one `else` branch that always prints the `fprintd-delete $USER` advice:

```diff
-elif $already_enrolled; then
-  # Rerunning setup would skip enrollment again while that print exists.
+else
+  # Rerunning setup skips enrollment while any print exists, including the one
+  # this run may just have enrolled.
   echo -e "\e[31m\nVerification failed. To enroll again, remove the saved fingerprints with\e[0m"
   echo -e "\e[31mfprintd-delete $USER, then run this setup again.\e[0m"
-else
-  echo -e "\e[31m\nVerification failed. You may want to try enrolling again.\e[0m"
 fi
```

this reproducer prints `ok - a fresh print that fails to verify says how to enroll again` (exit 0), and the PR's `test/shell.d/fingerprint-setup-enrolled-test.sh` still prints its four `ok` lines (exit 0).
</details>

### Package test runs the host's `fprintd-list`

`fingerprint-package-test.sh` does not stub `fprintd-list`, which setup now calls before enrolling. **Impact:** it fails wherever the current user has a print enrolled.

**Suggested change:** add an `fprintd-list` stub that prints `User $1 has no fingers enrolled for Test Sensor.`.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at 2b24db05)</summary>

# Reproducer: fingerprint-package-test.sh now depends on the host's fprintd-list

Reviewed head: `2b24db055dbf71cb5e152d3f131f36481ebda988`. Merge-base: `97a9fce54f5df007afe7b8637ddc09314f38ad00`.

`test/shell.d/fingerprint-package-test.sh` runs the real setup script with stubs for `sudo`, `pacman`, `fprintd-enroll` and `fprintd-verify`, but not `fprintd-list`. The PR's setup now calls `fprintd-list "$USER"` before enrolling, so the test reaches whatever `fprintd-list` is on the developer's PATH. This script stands in for a machine where the current user already has a print enrolled, by putting an `fprintd-list` that prints fprintd's enrolled format behind the test's own stub directories. Run from the repository root:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Run from the repository root. Stands in for a machine where the current user
# already has a print enrolled: fprintd-list reports it in fprintd's format.
set -euo pipefail
host=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$host"' EXIT
cat > "$host/fprintd-list" <<'STUB'
#!/bin/bash
printf 'Fingerprints for user %s on Test Sensor (press):\n - #0: right-index-finger\n' "$1"
STUB
chmod +x "$host/fprintd-list"
PATH="$host:$PATH" bash test/shell.d/fingerprint-package-test.sh
```

## Actual output at 2b24db05 (exit 1, stderr)

```
not ok - setup stops on the simulated enrollment or installation failure
```

Setup took the new already-enrolled path, skipped the stubbed `fprintd-enroll`, got a failure from the stubbed `fprintd-verify`, printed the `fprintd-delete` advice and exited 0, which the test treats as a failure.

## Actual output at the merge-base 97a9fce5 (exit 0)

```
ok - a fresh machine installs libfprint-git and reaches enrollment
ok - installed stock libfprint is replaced without a removal step
ok - a rerun with everything installed goes straight to enrollment
ok - a failed installation stops before enrollment
ok - missing hardware performs no package operations
```

## With the suggested change

Adding an `fprintd-list` stub to `test/shell.d/fingerprint-package-test.sh`:

```diff
@@ -45,6 +45,10 @@
   *) printf 'pacman %s\n' "$*" >> "$CALL_LOG"; exit 99 ;;
 esac
 STUB
+cat > "$scratch/bin/fprintd-list" <<'STUB'
+#!/bin/bash
+echo "User $1 has no fingers enrolled for Test Sensor."
+STUB
 cat > "$scratch/bin/fprintd-enroll" <<'STUB'
 #!/bin/bash
 # Stop before verification/PAM; no host authentication files may be changed.
```

the same script prints the five `ok` lines above at 2b24db05 (exit 0).
</details>

<details><summary>More findings</summary>

### The `enroll-duplicate` premise does not match fprintd's source (not reproduced)

Since fprintd 1.92.0 (commit `f398d09`, "device: Delete existing print in EnrollStart"), `EnrollStart` deletes the same user's existing print for the requested finger before its duplicate check (`src/device.c:2203-2220` in 1.94.5). So a right-index print left by an earlier `sudo fprintd-enroll "$USER"` does not by itself cause `enroll-duplicate`: fprintd deletes it and enrolls the finger again. `enroll-duplicate` needs the scanned finger to match a different stored print, for example:
- the same finger stored for `$USER` under another finger name: `fprintd-list "$USER"` lists it, so this PR fixes that case;
- the same finger stored for another account on the same reader: `fprintd-list "$USER"` shows nothing, and setup still ends at "Enrollment failed".

The output quoted in #13433 came from `fprintd-enroll right-index-finger`, which fprintd reads as a username (`-f` selects the finger). Source reading only; not run against fprintd or hardware.

**Suggested change:** reword the code comment at `bin/omarchy-setup-security-fingerprint:92-94` (and the PR description) to describe when fprintd reports `enroll-duplicate`, and if possible confirm with the output of the setup's own `sudo fprintd-enroll "$USER"` on the affected machine.
</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified** (sandboxed tests with stubbed fprintd and `sudo`):
- With a print listed by `fprintd-list`, setup skips `fprintd-enroll`, runs `fprintd-verify` and writes PAM; with none listed, it still enrolls.
- A failed enrollment still exits 1 before any PAM change.
- The new test fails when copied onto the merge-base (`not ok - an enrolled print is not enrolled again`) and passes at the head (4 `ok`).
- `^ *- #[0-9]+: ` matches only the entry lines of fprintd 1.94.5 `utils/list.c`, whose output is not translated. The `has [0-9]+ fingerprints? enrolled` pattern in #13467 never matches it.

**Optional test improvement:** the positive cases only check `sudo tee /etc/pam.d/omarchy-lock-fingerprint`, so deleting the `setup_pam_config` call on the verify-success branch still passes all four cases (sudo and polkit PAM never checked). Running setup from a copy with `/etc/pam.d/` pointed at a scratch stack, as `security-fingerprint-remove-test.sh` does, allows asserting the `sudo` and `polkit-1` edits too; that version caught the mutant.

**Related open PRs:** #13467 fixes the same issue and edits the same lines, so only one of the two can apply as is. #13612 also targets #13433 and adds a similar `fprintd-list` stub to the package test.
</details>
